newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst to list shares on NYSE on Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst to list shares on NYSE on Sept 24.

text.p: Hoechst AG, the German chemicals and pharmaceuticals group, said on Wednesday that it would list its shares on the New York stock exchange in September but that no new shares would be issued at this time.
Europe's largest chemicals group had last year announced plans to let Hoechst shares, currently traded on most major European exchanges, be listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
On Wednesday the group said the official start of trading was scheduled for September 24.
Hoechst again confirmed that the listing process would not involve the issue of new shares or the placement of existing shares in the company.
U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch will advise Hoechst on the deal while the Bank of New York will serve as the chemical group's depositary bank.
American Depositary Receipts, each representing one ordinary share of Hoechst, will be quoted on the New York Stock Exchange. The group's listing symbol which has been HAG will be changed to HOE.
Hoechst's decision to have its shares traded in the U.S. is part of a growing trend among German companies to broaden their investor base by seeking listing on U.S. exchanges.

Daimler-Benz was the first German company to list on the New York Stock Exchange and it has been joined by Deutsche Telekom and former Hoechst unit SGL Carbon. Diversified utility VEBA AG plans to list its shares in the U.S. in October.
